answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% component-spend reduction this cycle. The incumbent has refused to reopen price (memory_c4 confirms incumbents can move on price, but only when we have leverage to renegotiate — and we currently don't). The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so we must act. memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, and the line is running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer — meaning we cannot afford the longer validation timeline of a second-source qualification. Memory_c4 supports the expectation that a switch creates a credible renewal negotiation lever, but with a 14-day clock and a cost-cut mandate, switching primary is the action that directly minimizes TCO without expanding delivery risk on a path we've already proven. Verification of c2 and c4 confirms the low-cost vendor's prior performance and the feasibility of incumbent renegotiation as a fallback before committing.
